Its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. {{nihongo|'''Ōke Shrine'''|大毛神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

It is the "Ōke Shrine" of {{ill|Haguri District|hu|Haguri körzet|ja|葉栗郡|ko|하구리군 (아이치현)|pl|Powiat Haguri|sr|Област Хагури|zh|葉栗郡|qid=Q1032507}}, {{ill|Owari Province|Q514506|qid=Q514506}}, listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha register}}.

== Overview ==
*Founded in {{ill|899|Q23734|qid=Q23734}} (Shōtai 2).
*In the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}, it was called "Rokusha Myōjin" and "Rokusho Myōjin."
*It was also called "Hinagata no Miya." This is said to be because a doll associated with Imperial Princess Iori-iri-hime (daughter of {{ill|Emperor Keikō|Q329723|qid=Q329723}}) was enshrined here. Since the local place name is Iori-zuka and old sites linked with Ōke Shrine include An-iri-zuka, Tenshi-zuka, and Emperor Keikō's tomb (Haguri history records), it is said to have deep ties to Emperor Keikō and Princess Iori-iri-hime.
*In {{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}} (Meiji 5), it reverted to the old name Ōke Shrine and became a village shrine.
*In {{ill|1925|Q18107|qid=Q18107}} (Taishō 14), it became a gōsha.

== Enshrined deity ==
*{{ill|Ōgetsuhime|es|Ōgetsuhime|ja|オオゲツヒメ|zh|大宜都比賣|qid=Q3261482|lt=Ōgetsuhime-no-Mikoto}}

Though not an official enshrined deity, Princess Iori-iri-hime is also worshipped.

== Transportation ==
*5 minutes on foot from "Ōke" bus stop on {{ill|Meitetsu Bus|ja|名鉄バス|qid=Q6810397}}
**From {{ill|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|de|Bahnhof Meitetsu Ichinomiya|eo|Stacio Meitetsu-Ichinomiya|fr|Gare de Meitetsu Ichinomiya|id|Stasiun Meitetsu-Ichinomiya|ja|名鉄一宮駅|jv|Setatsiyun Meitetsu-Ichinomiya|ko|메이테쓰이치노미야역|ur|میئی ٹیسو اچینومیا اسٹیشن|zh|名鐵一宮站|qid=Q2856589}} / {{ill|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|arz|محطة اوارى ايكينوميا|de|Bahnhof Owari-Ichinomiya|eo|Stacio Owari-Ichinomiya|fr|Gare d'Owari-Ichinomiya|id|Stasiun Owari-Ichinomiya|it|Stazione di Owari-Ichinomiya|ja|尾張一宮駅|jv|Setatsiyun Owari-Ichinomiya|ko|오와리이치노미야역|ur|اوواری اچی نومیا اسٹیشن|zh|尾張一宮車站|qid=Q871495}} (platform 3 at Meitetsu Ichinomiya bus terminal), bound for "Yamasato Nishi" or "{{ill|Twin Arch 138|ja|ツインアーチ138|qid=Q11318660|lt=138 Tower Park}}"
